MEDICATION GUIDE — Apixaban (Eliquis) Tablets
Read this Medication Guide before you start taking apixaban and each time you get a refill.
What is the most important information I should know about apixaban?
• Do not stop taking apixaban without talking to the doctor who prescribes it. Stopping increases your risk of stroke.
• Apixaban can cause serious bleeding, which may lead to death. You may bruise more easily, and bleeding may take longer to stop.
Get medical help right away if you have: unexpected or heavy bleeding; red, pink, or brown urine; red or black stools that look like tar; coughing up blood or vomiting blood.
How should I take apixaban? Take apixaban exactly as prescribed, 2 times every day, with or without food. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day, then go back to your regular schedule. Do not take 2 doses at the same time.
Tell all your doctors and dentists that you take apixaban before any surgery or procedure.
Distributed by: Example Pharma, Inc. Revised: 03/2026. For more information, call 1-800-555-0126.

Advance Care Planning: Health Care Power of Attorney and Living Will
An advance directive is a legal document that lets you state your wishes for medical care if you become unable to make decisions for yourself. A Health Care Power of Attorney names a person (your health care agent) to make medical decisions for you if you cannot. A Living Will states which treatments you would or would not want at the end of life, such as a breathing machine or a feeding tube. These forms must be signed according to your state's rules, which often require witnesses or a notary.
Having aphasia does not mean you cannot make your own decisions. Your speech-language pathologist can help you understand the forms and communicate your choices.
Free forms are available from your state. For help completing the forms, call Triangle Legal Help at (919) 555-0137.

Re: Driving After Stroke
Dear Mr. Leon Fraser,
Following your stroke, your physician, Dr. Ravi Patel, recommends that you do not drive until you complete a formal driving evaluation. Stroke can affect vision, reaction time, attention, and judgment, even when you feel ready to drive.
A certified driver rehabilitation specialist at Safe Roads Driver Rehab will complete a clinical assessment (about 1.5 hours) and an on-road test (about 1 hour). Most insurance plans do not cover the evaluation; the cost is $450. Call (919) 555-0140 to schedule.
Bring your driver's license, glasses, and a list of your medications.
You will receive a written report. It may recommend driving with restrictions, adaptive equipment, more training, or stopping driving.
Until then, please arrange other transportation. Triangle Ride Access offers door-to-door rides: (919) 555-0141.
